page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz with x86_64 architecture. The server provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 8.0 GB of RAM (reflecting a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU), and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. It includes no local storage, requiring attached network storage volumes, and has no hardware GPUs or included public IPv4 addresses. Hardware instruction support covers AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate notable single-threaded strength. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server scores 3113.58, placing it in the top 10%, while Geekbench single-core reaches 2018.0 points in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing is also strong at 2531.0 points. Conversely, multithreaded capacity and throughput tasks fall into mid-tier or lower tiers due to the 4-vCPU limit, with stress-ng multi-core (6231.31) and PassMark CPU (7656.52) landing in the middle 50%. Decompression, Clang software compilation, PassMark database operations, and static web serving throughput (5.45 GB/sec) rank in the bottom 25%.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance and superior per-core execution speeds, the ecs.c8ae.xlarge provides efficient resource utilization for single-thread bound workloads, small backend microservices, batch processing, and dedicated compute utilities where vast memory pools or intensive multi-core parallelization are not required.

Powered by KVM virtualization, it is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no onboard local storage and no GPU accelerators. The CPU features AVX-512 vector extensions with BF16 and VNNI instruction support alongside cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core CPU throughput, while multithreaded and memory-intensive metrics perform near market median or lower quartiles due to the 4-vCPU capacity. This makes the ecs.c8ae.xlarge best suited for compute-focused tasks requiring elevated single-thread responsiveness, API endpoints, microservices, and lightweight batch processing.
